body:
Adds CHOPPAH as row 91 of **1.1.4. Independent & Original Engine Firmwares**, in the format the table uses.

CHOPPAH turns the M-VAVE FM-1 into an Amen break chopper: eight classic breaks cut into sixteen slices on the white keys, hold a key to loop it, and the black keys are momentary effect pads (roll, reverse, freeze, tape stop, gate, random, filter, dub throw). A generator rearranges the break live, with a four-slot master FX chain, sixteen patterns with a step sequencer, a synthesised kick, snare and hat, MIDI and a DJ filter.

- Repository: https://github.com/profikid/fm1-break-choppah
- Web installer: https://profikid.github.io/fm1-break-choppah/install/
- The firmware in a browser: https://profikid.github.io/fm1-break-choppah/emu/
- Manual: https://profikid.github.io/fm1-break-choppah/manual/
- Releases: https://github.com/profikid/fm1-break-choppah/releases

It is built on `fm1-base` (Charles Vestal) and `felucca-bsp` (Leo Kuroshita) and is MPL-2.0.

One note worth having in the table: CHOPPAH accepts both flash parts - the stock Puya P25Q80 and the UC25HQ80 that the units sold since autumn 2026 carry - so it installs and saves on those as well.

The firmware's own breaks are commercial recordings and are not covered by the repository's licence; the firmware source itself is MPL-2.0.
